title: How to set a due date in Linear on Mac: Shift D and the command bar
metaTitle: How to set a due date in Linear on Mac (Shift D)
description: How to set a due date in Linear on Mac: select an issue, press Shift D, or run Set Due Date from the ⌘K command bar. Steps for the desktop app.
targetKeyword: how to set a due date in linear on mac
secondaryKeywords: linear command bar set due date
intro: To set a due date in Linear on Mac, select the issue and press ⇧D (Shift D). Linear opens a date picker, and the day you choose becomes the issue's due date.
tldr: Select the issue, press ⇧D (Shift D), and pick the day in the date picker.
Older guides say ⌘D. Linear moved the due date shortcut to ⇧D in June 2021.
Press ⌘K, type due, and choose Set Due Date if you forget the key.
Remove a date with ⌘⇧D only after you test it, because Linear's docs did not confirm it.
Turn on due date under Display options, Issue view, Display properties to see dates on the list or board.

blocks.text: The keyboard is the fastest way to set a due date in Linear on Mac. Once you know the key, you can date a whole queue of issues without leaving the list. This page starts with that route, then covers the command bar, the right-click menu, the settings that make dates visible, and the mistakes that cost people time.
Set a due date with ⇧D on the Mac

Start by selecting the issue. You can open the issue in full view, or highlight it in a list or board. Press ↑ or ↓, or J or K, to move the highlight to the right row. Then press ⇧D. Linear opens a date picker, and the day you pick becomes the due date.

The key is Shift, not Command. That detail matters more than it sounds. Linear's June 3, 2021 changelog says the shortcut for setting an issue due date changed from ⌘D to ⇧D. If you learned the shortcut from a 2020 tutorial, your fingers may press the wrong key.

One trap catches almost everyone. If the cursor is blinking inside the title or the description, Shift D types a capital D into the text. Click an empty part of the view so the cursor leaves the text, then select the issue and press ⇧D again.

Watch the picker after you press the shortcut. Linear's 2020 due dates changelog confirms that the date picker opens. I could not open a page that lists the picker's exact controls, so read what is on your screen before you click.
Set a due date from the ⌘K command bar

If the shortcut slips your mind, use the command bar. Press ⌘K to open it, type due, and choose Set Due Date from the results. Linear's Select issues docs say ⌘K opens the command bar. The 2020 changelog also names Set Due Date as a way in.

The command bar helps in two cases. The first is when you cannot remember whether the key is ⌘D or ⇧D. The second is when you want a route that needs no memory at all. The command name stays the same, so searching for it is a dependable fallback. If the command bar is new to you, [open the command menu in Linear](/how-to/open-the-command-menu-in-linear) walks through it.
Set a due date with the right-click menu

Right-click is the third route. Select the issue, then right-click it. Linear's Select issues docs say right-click opens a contextual menu for the selected issues. The 2020 changelog lists right-click as an option too. Look for the due date item in that menu.

The label can change because Linear updates its app often. Read the menu before you click, and do not trust an old screenshot. If you select several issues first, check one result before you assume the rest changed too.
Why older guides tell you to press ⌘D

Linear's due dates changelog from October 22, 2020 says you can add a due date with ⌘D while viewing an issue. It also says the same works with an issue selected on a board or list. Many guides copied that line and never updated it.

Linear's June 3, 2021 entry replaced that key. Since then, ⇧D has been the shortcut for setting a due date. I could not confirm what ⌘D does in Linear today, so do not use it for dates. Use ⇧D instead.
Remove a due date in Linear on Mac

To remove a due date, select the issue and press ⌘⇧D. A third-party ShortcutFoo cheat sheet lists ⌘⇧D as Remove due date in its Issues II section. Linear's own docs did not confirm that shortcut in the pages I checked, so test it on a spare issue first.

If ⌘⇧D does nothing, open the date picker with ⇧D and look for a way to clear the date. I could not confirm the clear control, so read the picker before you choose. Do not delete the issue to get rid of a date. That is a much bigger change than you need.
Show due dates on your list or board

Setting a date does nothing for you if you cannot see it. Linear's Display options docs list due date among the issue properties you can show or hide. The path is Display options, then Issue view, then Display properties. Turn on due date there.

Some properties appear only in certain views, or only when related features are on. If due date is missing after you turn it on, switch views and look again. Start with the Display options control in your list or board view.
Once due date is on, each issue row can carry its date. That makes overdue work easy to spot. It also helps when you want the issues due this week in one glance.
What Linear shows for due dates in notifications
Linear's changelog index lists a November 5, 2026 change. Issue due date notifications now say when an issue is due, for example Due today. Sidebar due dates use a shorter format, such as Oct 9.

I could not open the full November 5 entry, so I cannot tell you every place the new wording appears. Set a test date that is due today, then check the notification text. If it reads differently, check that the app has updated and compare again.
Set due dates on several issues at once

Selecting several issues works the way the docs describe. Shift click selects one issue. Shift with an arrow key extends the selection. Command A selects all issues on the current list or board after filtering. Esc clears the selection. Those keys come from Linear's Select issues docs.

The docs I checked do not say clearly that Shift D applies to every selected issue. Test with two issues first. If only one changes, set the rest one at a time. The [selection guide](/how-to/select-multiple-issues-in-linear) covers more key patterns.
Set a due date while you create an issue

Press C to open issue creation on Mac. Linear's creating issues docs list C for that. Those docs do not show a due date field in the composer, and I could not verify the three-dot menu that some sources mention. Look at the composer for a date option first.

If you do not see a date option, save the issue, then select it and press ⇧D. The same docs say Esc closes the composer and asks whether to save a draft. So if you press Esc midway through a date, check the draft before you move on.
Recurring issues need a first due date

A recurring issue works differently. When you convert an issue to a recurring one, you choose a first due date and a cadence. The next issue is created at 00:01 the following day in the team's timezone, after the due date passes.
The timezone belongs to the team, not to your Mac. If you work in a different zone from your team, the day can seem off by one. Check the team's timezone before you trust the first date you pick.
Common mistakes when setting due dates

items: Pressing ⌘D and expecting a date picker. That shortcut is outdated for due dates.
Typing a capital D into a title because the cursor was still in the text.
Selecting several issues and assuming every one received the date.
Looking for the date but leaving due date off in Display properties.
Trusting ⌘⇧D to remove a date without testing it on a spare issue first.

blocks.text: Mac app and web app: what I could not confirm

This guide follows Linear's public docs and changelog. It does not follow a Mac-only walkthrough, because I found none. I found no menu paths for the date picker in the Mac app, and no version numbers for the desktop app. Linear's changelog is dated, not versioned, so this guide uses dates instead.

I also found no note that due dates behave differently on the web app. Treat these steps as desktop app steps, and test each one once. A quick test costs far less than fixing a batch of issues with the wrong date.
Check the date and sort your work by it

After you set a date, open the issue and read the sidebar. The due date should show there in the short format. If the date is wrong, press ⇧D again. The picker should open again, so you can correct the day.

Dates are only useful when you can sort by them. [Filter issues in Linear](/how-to/filter-issues-in-linear) explains views and saved filters. Keep the views you check each day in one place, so the due dates stay in front of you.

faq.question: What is the shortcut to set a due date in Linear on Mac?
faq.answer: Select the issue, then press ⇧D (Shift D). Linear's June 3, 2021 changelog says the shortcut changed from ⌘D to ⇧D, so ⇧D is the current key for setting an issue due date.

faq.question: Why does ⌘D no longer set a due date?
faq.answer: Linear's October 22, 2020 changelog listed ⌘D for due dates. The June 2021 changelog moved the shortcut to ⇧D. Guides written before then still show ⌘D, so they are out of date.

faq.question: How do I remove a due date in Linear on Mac?
faq.answer: Try ⌘⇧D with the issue selected. A third-party cheat sheet lists it as Remove due date, but I could not confirm it in Linear's docs. Test it on a spare issue first.

faq.question: Why can't I see due dates on my board?
faq.answer: Open Display options, go to Issue view, then Display properties, and turn on due date. Some properties appear only in certain views, so check the view you are in too.

faq.question: Can I set a due date from the command bar?
faq.answer: Yes. Press ⌘K, type due, and choose Set Due Date. Linear's Select issues docs say ⌘K opens the command bar.

faq.question: How do due dates look in notifications now?
faq.answer: Linear's changelog index says a November 5, 2026 update made issue due date notifications say when an issue is due, such as Due today. Sidebar due dates use a shorter format, such as Oct 9.

faq.question: Is there a Mac-only menu path for due dates?
faq.answer: I found no Mac-only walkthrough with menu paths for the date picker. The steps here come from Linear's docs, its changelog, and a third-party cheat sheet. Confirm the picker layout on your own screen.

faq.question: What time is a recurring issue created?
faq.answer: The next issue is created at 00:01 the following day in the team's timezone, after the due date passes. Linear's creating issues docs say so.

steps.name: Select the issue
steps.text: Open the issue, or highlight it in a list or board. Press ↑ or ↓, or J or K, until the right row is highlighted. The highlighted issue is the one that receives the date.
steps.tip: Check the highlight before you press a key. The shortcut acts on the highlighted issue.

steps.name: Press Shift D
steps.text: Press ⇧D, which is Shift and D together. Linear opens a date picker for that issue. Linear's 2020 due dates changelog describes this picker.
steps.tip: A capital D in the title means the cursor was in a text field. Click an empty part of the view and try again.

steps.name: Pick the day
steps.text: Choose the day in the picker. I could not open a page that lists the picker's exact controls, so read the screen before you click. Pick the real deadline, not a guess.
steps.tip: Pressing ⇧D again opens the picker again, so you can correct a wrong date.

steps.name: Confirm the date
steps.text: Open the issue and look for the due date in its details. The sidebar uses a short date format, such as Oct 9. If the date is missing, use the display steps below.
steps.tip: A short date in the sidebar is the due date, not the date the issue was created.

steps.name: Open the command bar
steps.text: Press ⌘K to open the command bar. Type due, then choose Set Due Date. Linear's Select issues docs say ⌘K opens the command bar, so your screen should match.
steps.tip: Use this route when you cannot remember whether the key is ⌘D or ⇧D.

steps.name: Use the right-click menu
steps.text: Select the issue, then right-click it. Linear's docs say right-click opens a contextual menu for selected issues. Look for the due date item and choose it.
steps.tip: Labels can change as Linear updates its app. Read the menu before you click.

steps.name: Remove a due date
steps.text: Select the issue and press ⌘⇧D. A third-party ShortcutFoo cheat sheet lists this as Remove due date. Linear's docs did not confirm it, so try it on a spare issue first.
steps.tip: If nothing happens, open the picker with ⇧D and look for a clear option.

steps.name: Turn on due date in the view
steps.text: Open Display options from your list or board view. Go to Issue view, then Display properties. Turn on due date so it shows on each issue.
steps.tip: Some properties appear only in certain views. Switch views if due date is still missing.

troubleshooting.problem: Pressing ⌘D does nothing useful or opens something else
troubleshooting.fix: Linear changed the due date shortcut from ⌘D to ⇧D in June 2021. Use ⇧D. If ⌘D still triggers something else on your Mac, that comes from another app or system setting, which I did not check.

troubleshooting.problem: Shift D types a capital D into the title
troubleshooting.fix: The cursor is inside a text field. Click an empty part of the view, select the issue, and press ⇧D again.

troubleshooting.problem: The due date is missing from the list or board
troubleshooting.fix: Open Display options, go to Issue view, then Display properties, and turn on due date. Some properties appear only in certain views, so check the view as well.
That shortcut came from a third-party cheat sheet, not Linear's docs. Open the date picker with ⇧D and look for a clear control there.

troubleshooting.problem: Only one of several selected issues got the date
troubleshooting.fix: I could not confirm that due date applies to every selected issue. Set the rest one at a time with ⇧D, and check each one.
